defectFoundAndFixed.symptom: After a governed share was granted, the recipient's recall returned 0 hits for a multi-word query, even though the store's own search returned the same entry for the author. A granted fact was invisible exactly when it was needed.
defectFoundAndFixed.rootCause: The shared-entry filter matched the ENTIRE query as one lowercased substring (entry.content.toLowerCase().includes(wantText)), while the SQLite store tokenizes the query and matches any token. A multi-word query ('unique marker persona alpha') never appears contiguously in the content, so it never matched.
defectFoundAndFixed.fix: Added ONE tokenizer, tokenizeMemoryText, in core/src/memory/model.ts. The store's tokenize now delegates to it, and the runtime's shared-entry filter uses tokens.some(token => entry.content.toLowerCase().includes(token)) — identical semantics to the store, so a share can never be recalled through a stricter rule than the source bucket.
defectFoundAndFixed.rawAfter: bravo after share 200 1 ["The unique marker ALPHA_SECRET belongs to persona Alpha private ledger."]

A_private_write_is_private.statement: A subagent-scoped write (POST /memory/write {scope:'subagent', scopeId:'alpha'}) is recalled by its author and NEVER by a neighbour.

evidence.unknownPersonaWrite: rememberForSubagent('ghost', ...) -> ok:false (a fact scoped to an unknown persona is refused, never orphaned)

B_prompt_composition_nonleak.statement: The non-leak reaches the COMPOSED PROMPT: a turn composed for scope 'subagent:bravo' never carries persona alpha's private fact; the same turn for 'subagent:alpha' does, in the ## Recalled memory DATA section.

evidence.bravo: composeTurnPrompt('what is the unique marker for persona alpha', {scope:'subagent:bravo'}).text does NOT contain 'ALPHA_SECRET'
evidence.wiring: the prompt-composer memory port calls recallForSubagent for a 'subagent:<id>' scope (core/src/runtime.ts)

C_governed_specific_share.statement: A governed share names ONE entry from ONE persona to ONE persona, backed by a REAL KAI approval. The default policy PARKS it for a human (memory.share is deliberately NOT in KAI_INTERNAL_STATE_TOOLS); nothing is granted while parked. There is no broad 'grant everything' shape.

D_recipient_gets_only_shared_item.statement: After approval, the recipient CAN recall the shared fact and ONLY the explicitly shared item — never the rest of the source's bucket.

F_restart_persistence.statement: A real restart (a NEW Core over the SAME database file and the SAME JSON files) keeps alpha's private facts, keeps the shared fact shared, and keeps the unshared fact private.

conclusion: The per-subagent memory isolation property is pinned: A, C, D, E, F and every listed negative case are END-TO-END PROVEN (through the real Core API handler, real runtime, real SQLite and real JSON persistence); B (prompt-composition non-leak) is INTEGRATION PROVEN.
